```{r cleaning-function}
# Function: clean_air_quality
# Purpose: Clean one air quality dataset and calculate
#          average daily pollutant concentrations.

# Arguments:
# file_path = location of the CSV file
# ozone_units = desired units for ozone (ppm or ppb)

# Returns:
# A cleaned tibble containing one row per date with
# daily average CO, PM2.5, and O3 concentrations.

clean_air_quality <- function(file_path, ozone_units = "ppm") {

  # Step 1: Read the CSV file
  aq <- read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

  # Step 2: Rename columns to make them easier to use
  aq <- aq %>%
    rename(
      date = Date,
      co = `Daily Max 8-hour CO Concentration`,
      pm25 = `Daily Mean PM2.5 Concentration`,
      o3 = `Daily Max 8-hour Ozone Concentration`
    )

  # Step 3: Convert the date variable into Date format
  # mdy() recognizes dates written as month/day/year
  aq <- aq %>%
    mutate(date = mdy(date))

  # Step 4: Remove exact duplicate rows
  # This prevents identical records from being counted twice
  aq <- aq %>%
    distinct()

  # Step 5: Replace negative pollutant values with zero
  # A for loop applies the same correction to all pollutants
  for (pollutant in c("co", "pm25", "o3")) {

    aq[[pollutant]] <- ifelse(
      !is.na(aq[[pollutant]]) & aq[[pollutant]] < 0,
      0,
      aq[[pollutant]]
    )
  }

  # Step 6: Calculate the average concentration for each date
  # Missing values are excluded from the calculation
  aq <- aq %>%
    group_by(date) %>%
    summarise(
      across(
        c(co, pm25, o3),
        ~ if (all(is.na(.x))) {
          NA_real_
        } else {
          mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
        }
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # Step 7: Convert ozone from ppm to ppb if requested
  # 1 ppm = 1000 ppb
  if (ozone_units == "ppb") {
    aq <- aq %>%
      mutate(o3 = o3 * 1000)
  }

  # Step 8: Return the cleaned dataset
  return(aq)
}
```


```{r test-function, include=FALSE}
# Apply the cleaning function to the 2018 dataset
aq_2018 <- clean_air_quality("AQ_2018.csv")

# Display the first six rows of the cleaned dataset
head(aq_2018)

# Check the structure of the cleaned dataset
glimpse(aq_2018)

# Check that each date appears only once
anyDuplicated(aq_2018$date)
```


```{r combine-data, include=FALSE}
# Apply the cleaning function to the remaining years
# Ozone is kept in ppm (the function's default).

aq_2019 <- clean_air_quality("AQ_2019.csv")
aq_2020 <- clean_air_quality("AQ_2020.csv")

# Combine the three cleaned datasets into one tibble
# bind_rows() stacks the datasets vertically.
aq_all <- bind_rows(aq_2018, aq_2019, aq_2020)

# Create year and month variables from the date
# These will be useful for our tables and plots.
aq_all <- aq_all %>%
  mutate(
    year = year(date),
    month = month(date)
  )

# Preview the combined dataset
head(aq_all)

# Examine the number of observations and variables
dim(aq_all)
```


```{r validate-data, include=FALSE}
# Check that each date appears only once
anyDuplicated(aq_all$date)

# Count the number of observations for each year
aq_all %>%
  count(year)

# Check for missing values in each variable
colSums(is.na(aq_all))

# Check whether any negative concentrations remain
aq_all %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      c(co, pm25, o3),
      ~ sum(.x < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )
```

```{r}
# Group observations by year and calculate the
# minimum and maximum for each pollutant.

aq_summary <- aq_all %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    # Carbon monoxide
    co_min = min(co, na.rm = TRUE),
    co_max = max(co, na.rm = TRUE),

    # Fine particulate matter
    pm25_min = min(pm25, na.rm = TRUE),
    pm25_max = max(pm25, na.rm = TRUE),

    # Ozone
    o3_min = min(o3, na.rm = TRUE),
    o3_max = max(o3, na.rm = TRUE),

    .groups = "drop"
  )
```


```{r annual-tables}
# Function to generate a summary table for each year
make_year_table <- function(selected_year) {

  # Extract summary statistics for the selected year
  year_data <- aq_summary %>%
    filter(year == selected_year)

  # Organize the results by pollutant
  year_table <- tibble(
    Pollutant = c("CO (ppm)",
                  "PM2.5 (µg/m³)",
                  "O3 (ppm)"),

    Minimum = c(year_data$co_min,
                year_data$pm25_min,
                year_data$o3_min),

    Maximum = c(year_data$co_max,
                year_data$pm25_max,
                year_data$o3_max)
  )

  # Format the table to three decimal places
  kable(
    year_table,
    digits = 3,
    format.args = list(nsmall = 3),
    caption = paste(
      "Minimum and Maximum Daily Pollutant Concentrations:",
      selected_year
    )
  )
}
```

## Annual Summary Statistics

```{r table-2018}

make_year_table(2018)
```

*Note: Data for 2020 are limited to January–April.*


```{r}
# Convert CO and O3 concentrations into long format
# so both pollutants can be included in one plot.
monthly_co_o3 <- aq_all %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(co, o3),
    names_to = "pollutant",
    values_to = "concentration"
  ) %>%

  # Group by calendar month and pollutant, pooling all years
  group_by(month, pollutant) %>%

  # Calculate monthly summary statistics
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(concentration)),
    avg = mean(concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  # Calculate standard error and 95% confidence limits
  mutate(
    se = sd / sqrt(n),
    LB = avg - 1.96 * se,
    UB = avg + 1.96 * se,

    # Convert month numbers to abbreviated month names
    month = factor(month, levels = 1:12,
                   labels = month.abb),

    # Create readable pollutant labels
    pollutant = factor(pollutant,
                       levels = c("co", "o3"),
                       labels = c("CO", "O3"))
  )
```

## Monthly CO and Ozone Concentrations

```{r}
# Plot monthly means and 95% confidence intervals
plot1 <- ggplot(
  monthly_co_o3,
  aes(x = month, y = avg, color = pollutant)
) +

  # Display monthly mean concentrations as points
  geom_point(size = 3) +

  # Display the 95% confidence intervals
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = LB, ymax = UB),
    width = 0.2
  ) +

  # Separate pollutants using individual y-axis scales
  facet_wrap(~ pollutant, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +

  # Assign a distinct color to each pollutant
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("CO" = "pink2", "O3" = "green4")
  ) +

  # Add informative titles and axis labels
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Mean CO and Ozone Concentrations",
    subtitle = "RDU Airport, 2018–2020",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Mean Concentration (ppm)",
    color = "Pollutant"
  ) +

  # Apply a clean background
  theme_classic()

# Display the completed plot
plot1
```
Separate panels with independent y-axis scales were used because CO and O3 concentrations differ considerably in magnitude. This allows the monthly patterns and confidence intervals of both pollutants to be clearly visualized.

```{r}
# Group PM2.5 concentrations by year and month
monthly_pm25 <- aq_all %>%
  group_by(year, month) %>%

  # Calculate the mean daily PM2.5 concentration
  # for each month within each year
  summarise(
    avg = mean(pm25, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  # Convert month and year into categorical variables
  mutate(
    month = factor(month,
                   levels = 1:12,
                   labels = month.abb),
    year = factor(year)
  )
```

## Monthly PM2.5 Concentrations

```{r}
# Plot monthly PM2.5 concentrations by year
plot2 <- ggplot(
  monthly_pm25,
  aes(x = month, y = avg,
      color = year, group = year)
) +

  # Connect monthly averages within each year
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +

  # Display individual monthly averages
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +

  # Assign a different color to each year
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "2018" = "blue",
      "2019" = "hotpink",
      "2020" = "darkgreen"
    )
  ) +

  # Add informative titles and axis labels
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Mean PM2.5 Concentrations by Year",
    subtitle = "RDU Airport, 2018–2020",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Mean Concentration (µg/m³)",
    color = "Year"
  ) +

  # Apply a clean background
  theme_classic()

# Display the completed plot
plot2
```

A line graph with points was selected to show changes in monthly PM2.5 concentrations over time and facilitate comparisons of seasonal patterns across years.

## Interpretation

CO and ozone exhibited contrasting seasonal patterns, with CO concentrations generally higher during colder months and ozone concentrations peaking in June. PM2.5 concentrations showed no consistent seasonal pattern across years, although monthly concentrations steadily increased from January through April 2020, and 2020 had the highest maximum daily concentration of 31.200 $\mu g/m^3$. Comparisons involving 2020 should be interpreted cautiously because data were only available through April.
